title: SeatGeek × Ex-Grubhub | People who know marketplaces
intro: Why this network for SeatGeek? Grubhub and SeatGeek both depend on high-volume consumer journeys, reliable transaction systems, partner operations and exceptional experiences when something goes wrong. These six professionals have operated in parts of that environment. Each introduction below explains the specific transferable experience, the SeatGeek problem it could help solve, and the remaining fit question. These are editorial recommendations—not endorsements or confirmed applications.

items.note: WHY I WOULD INTRODUCE EDUARDO: He has led consumer product engineering organizations of up to 36 and modernization across 30+ services. SeatGeek needs enterprise ticketing products that can evolve without sacrificing reliability for venues and fans. Eduardo has led precisely the kind of multi-team modernization and delivery work that makes that possible in a complex consumer business. CHECK: Confirm the current director-level opening, enterprise product scope, location and reporting structure.

WHY I WOULD INTRODUCE CONNOR: He has taken platform and API products from concept to delivery and knows how interconnected marketplace services shape the end user experience. SeatGeek's fan journey depends on good product decisions across discovery, purchase and integrations—not only attractive screens. Connor offers a product builder's systems perspective. CHECK: Demonstrate direct consumer conversion and experimentation ownership, plus location eligibility.

WHY I WOULD INTRODUCE ELENA: She has handled large, messy enterprise implementations, data quality, onboarding and escalations, including deployments involving major national brands. Ticketing clients need someone who can make a complex rollout work across technical and operational teams, particularly when problems become urgent. That's Elena's transferable strength. CHECK: Confirm renewals/expansion ownership, sports or live-event domain requirements and travel.

WHY I WOULD INTRODUCE MIKE: He has led engineering across consumer homepages, search and discovery and shared platforms, including organizations of up to 45. In ticketing, discovery speed and platform stability influence both fan experience and conversion. Mike has managed engineering where those concerns meet, not only feature delivery. CHECK: Depth in core infrastructure, reliability engineering and SeatGeek's current stack.

WHY I WOULD INTRODUCE DANIEL: Across 13+ years at Grubhub, he helped build and lead driver app and post-purchase engineering across mobile and web. Once a customer has paid, the experience isn't finished: changes, uncertainty and support determine whether they trust the marketplace. SeatGeek has similarly time-sensitive post-purchase moments where Daniel's operational product perspective is relevant. CHECK: The SupportX team's specific technical remit, scale and engineering-management expectations.

items.role: Lead Product Manager, Fan Experience (secondary alignment)
items.note: WHY I WOULD INTRODUCE PAUL: He combines technical product ownership and decision science at Grubhub with AI product building, integrations and leadership at Unlocked Labs and TalentBot. SeatGeek has opportunities to improve relevance, decision support and friction in complex fan journeys; Paul can translate technical possibilities into shipped product. I would present him as a differentiated technical/AI product perspective, rather than claim proven ticketing-domain fit. CHECK: Direct consumer PM outcomes, experimentation depth and workplace/location constraints.
